# Adam Hamilton Watchdog File

**Subject:** Adam Hamilton, Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Kansas, 2026, challenging Republican Sen. Roger Marshall
**Compiled:** October 25, 2026 for the On Point Politics watchdog database, onpointpolitics.us
**Data cutoff:** FEC data through September 30, 2026 as compiled by VoteLog, the pre-general period through October 14, 2026 as reported by CQ Roll Call, and independent expenditures through October 22, 2026.
**Next scheduled data drop:** FEC 48 hour reports through Election Day and the post-general report due December 3, 2026.

## Bottom line up front

Hamilton is a first time candidate and the founding pastor of the Church of the Resurrection in Leawood, which a Kansas Reflector headline of July 22, 2026 calls the nation's largest Methodist church. He entered the race on April 30, 2026 and became one of the strongest Democratic fundraisers in the Senate map. A VoteLog compilation of FEC data shows $13,533,711 raised through September 30, 2026, of which $12,231,674 came from individuals and only $195,000 from PACs, https://votelog.org/investigations/kansas-senate-general-money. CQ Roll Call reported another $5.6 million from October 1 to 14, https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2026/oct/23/senate-democratic-candidates-keep-the-cash-flowing/.

Three money streams matter:

1. **Small and in-state donors.** His first four days brought $1.01 million from 6,700 donors, about 70 percent from Kansas, https://kansasreflector.com/2026/05/04/democrat-running-for-u-s-senate-receives-1-million-in-donations-in-campaigns-first-week/.
2. **Democratic Senate super PACs.** Groups counted as benefiting Hamilton include People Over Politics Action Fund at $9,657,045, WinSenate at $8,139,349 and Lower Costs Now at $2,933,659. WinSenate and Lower Costs Now are funded largely by SMP. Total outside money benefiting him was $27,771,284 through October 22, 2026, against $18,359,813 benefiting Marshall, per VoteLog.
3. **Farm country.** He has no farm money identified, but the farm bill, tariffs and diesel prices are the live decisions where his pitch to unaffiliated and Republican leaning farmers lands.

## Committee structure and treasurer

The authorized committee name, FEC committee ID and treasurer were not verified in this pass. Before launch, an Adam Hamilton Exploratory Committee took contributions through adamhamiltonexploratory.com, https://kansasreflector.com/2026/04/24/gop-ethics-complaint-says-kansas-city-area-pastor-improperly-used-church-resources/. Campaign manager Mike Phillips and spokesperson Tyson Brody speak for the campaign. VoteLog shows $1,016,500 in transfers from authorized committees, which points to at least one joint fundraising committee whose name was not found.

## Small donors

Documented. The campaign reported $1.01 million in its first four days, from 6,700 individuals with an average gift of $140. It said 92 percent of donors gave $100 or less and that gifts came from 68 of 105 counties. In its first 62 days it reported $3.66 million from about 16,000 people, https://kansasreflector.com/2026/07/08/kansas-democratic-candidate-for-u-s-senate-attracts-3-6m-in-two-months-of-campaigning/. A Political Wire headline reports a $10.6 million third quarter; that body was not read. VoteLog lists $50,206 of candidate self funding.

Inference: A base this wide gives no single donor leverage. The pressure points are the national groups that carry most of the paid media.

## Party and leadership

Documented. WinSenate and Lower Costs Now are both funded by SMP, which VoteLog shows giving $171,120,000 to WinSenate and $30,000,000 to Lower Costs Now across all races this cycle. FF PAC gave Lower Costs Now $20,000,000. KCUR, relaying another outlet on October 9, 2026, reported that a PAC associated with Sen. Chuck Schumer put $5 million into the race, https://www.kcur.org/politics-elections-and-government/2026-10-21/control-of-the-senate-goes-through-kansas-marshall-and-hamilton-clash-at-last-debate. Hamilton said at the final debate that he would not vote for Schumer as leader. Marshall says Schumer funded Hamilton and would make him beholden.

Inference: The leadership vote is the one lever where his stated position cuts against his largest outside funders. Watch whether that pledge survives January 2027.

## Ideological groups

Documented. People Over Politics Action Fund is the largest single outside spender on his side. Its top cycle funders are United Futures PAC at $6,250,000 and The Bench at $1,100,000. The Edge Action Fund, $2,475,000, and The 1861 Initiative, $1,461,683, also count as benefiting him. Their own donors were not traced.

## Own finances and disclosure history

No Senate candidate financial disclosure was retrieved. KCUR reports he was a Republican until earlier in 2026, https://www.kcur.org/news/2026-10-19/kansas-farmers-ranchers-roger-marshall-donald-trump-midterm. His income from the church, book royalties or speaking was not verified.

## Enforcement and controversies

- **FEC complaint, April 2026.** Kansas GOP executive director Rob Fillion filed an FEC complaint alleging the church made an in-kind contribution by letting Hamilton use church channels, citing a February 27 video on the church YouTube channel. Hamilton's spokesman said Marshall was attacking people of faith. The church said it keeps clear boundaries and will not use its data, facilities or staff for the campaign. No outcome was reported, https://kansasreflector.com/2026/04/24/gop-ethics-complaint-says-kansas-city-area-pastor-improperly-used-church-resources/.
- **2005 church camp report.** A Marshall campaign ad says Hamilton ignored parents and never called police after a 2005 report about a volunteer. Hamilton has said the 2005 inquiry was inconclusive and that he should have reported it to law enforcement. At the final debate he admitted a mistake in not checking whether the volunteer returned in 2006. Tall Oaks camp demanded the ad be suspended over an unauthorized photo; Marshall's staff said it was corrected, https://kansasreflector.com/2026/10/05/roger-marshalls-attack-ad-against-adam-hamilton-contains-unauthorized-image-of-children/.

## Deal table

| Interest | Money in | Ask | Lever | Stake | Decision date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Small donors | $12.2M individuals through Sept. 30 | Lower costs | Votes on costs, health care | Not quantified | 2027 |
| SMP network | WinSenate $8.1M, Lower Costs Now $2.9M benefiting | Senate majority | Leadership vote | Senate control | January 2027 |
| Ideological groups | People Over Politics $9.7M benefiting | Not stated | Floor votes | Not quantified | 2027 |
| Farmers | No farm money identified | Farm bill, tariff relief, diesel | Farm bill vote; tariff votes | $62B Kansas ag economy | Lame duck or 2027 |

## Levers and calendar

| Decision | Who holds it now | When | Which donors care |
|---|---|---|---|
| Farm bill | Senate after committee passage | Lame duck or 2027 | Farm groups |
| Tariffs and beef imports | President; Senate | Ongoing | Ranchers, grain farmers |
| ACA subsidies | Congress | 2027 | Health care and pharma |
| Senate leader | Democratic caucus | January 2027 | SMP network |
| AI regulation | Congress | 2027 | Tech, AI industry |

Calendar. Election November 3, 2026. Post-general FEC report December 3, 2026. New Congress and leadership votes January 2027. Farm bill floor action and appropriations through 2027.

## What we could not verify

- Committee name, FEC ID and treasurer; joint fundraising committee names.
- PAC donors, which VoteLog does not itemize; vendors and media buyers.
- The Q3 total, seen only in a headline at https://politicalwire.com/2026/10/13/adam-hamilton-reports-10-6-million-q3-haul/.
- Upstream donors of People Over Politics Action Fund beyond the top two, and the Schumer associated PAC named by KCUR.
- Senate financial disclosure, church compensation and book income.
- VoteLog does not name its publisher and its chart totals differ slightly from its tables; every VoteLog figure is Secondary.
- Bodies not read: https://politicalwire.com/2026/10/13/adam-hamilton-reports-10-6-million-q3-haul/ and https://www.dscc.org/article/dscc-statement-on-adam-hamiltons-victory-in-kansas-senate-primary/ and https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6166006-adam-hamilton-kansas-senate/

# Adam Hamilton research notes

Audit trail for KS-adam-hamilton, compiled October 25, 2026, on a budget of about five searches.

## Thread 1: Committees and totals

### Takeaway
Raised $13.5 million through September 30 and $5.6 million more in early October. Committee ID not verified.

### Cited findings
- Raised $13,533,711, spent $10,350,311, cash $3,183,400 through September 30, 2026; individuals $12,231,674, PACs $195,000, transfers $1,016,500, self $50,206. https://votelog.org/investigations/kansas-senate-general-money
- $1.01 million in first four days, 6,700 donors. https://kansasreflector.com/2026/05/04/democrat-running-for-u-s-senate-receives-1-million-in-donations-in-campaigns-first-week/
- $3.66 million from 16,000 people in 62 days. https://kansasreflector.com/2026/07/08/kansas-democratic-candidate-for-u-s-senate-attracts-3-6m-in-two-months-of-campaigning/
- $5.6 million from October 1 to 14. https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2026/oct/23/senate-democratic-candidates-keep-the-cash-flowing/
- Exploratory committee existed before launch. https://kansasreflector.com/2026/04/24/gop-ethics-complaint-says-kansas-city-area-pastor-improperly-used-church-resources/

### Inferences
- The $1 million in transfers implies a joint fundraising committee.

### Gaps
- FEC committee ID, treasurer, vendors.

## Thread 2: Outside money

### Takeaway
Outside money benefiting him totals about $27.8 million, but far more is spent attacking him than promoting him.

### Cited findings
- Supporting $3,157,660, opposing $16,082,094 through October 22, 2026; top groups listed. https://votelog.org/investigations/kansas-senate-general-money
- $590,000 in ad reservations for Hamilton against $2.3 million for Marshall as of October 2, AdImpact via AP. https://time.com/article/2026/10/07/why-kansas-has-emerged-as-a-new-battleground-state-and-why-it-matters/

### Gaps
- Upstream donors of People Over Politics Action Fund, The Edge Action Fund and The 1861 Initiative.

## Thread 3: Enforcement and controversies

### Cited findings
- Kansas GOP FEC complaint over church channels, with campaign and church responses. https://kansasreflector.com/2026/04/24/gop-ethics-complaint-says-kansas-city-area-pastor-improperly-used-church-resources/
- Marshall camp ad and Tall Oaks dispute. https://kansasreflector.com/2026/10/05/roger-marshalls-attack-ad-against-adam-hamilton-contains-unauthorized-image-of-children/
- Debate admission of a mistake about 2006. https://www.kcur.org/politics-elections-and-government/2026-10-21/control-of-the-senate-goes-through-kansas-marshall-and-hamilton-clash-at-last-debate

### Gaps
- FEC disposition of the complaint.

## Thread 4: Levers and positions

### Cited findings
- Positions on tariffs, Iran, ACA, Social Security cap, AI, Israel and Schumer. https://www.kcur.org/politics-elections-and-government/2026-10-21/control-of-the-senate-goes-through-kansas-marshall-and-hamilton-clash-at-last-debate
- Would have voted to advance the farm bill. https://www.kcur.org/news/2026-10-19/kansas-farmers-ranchers-roger-marshall-donald-trump-midterm

## Campaign intel

- **Main message.** He runs as an independent minded Democrat leading from the center, focused on pocketbook costs, and says there is room for Trump voters in his campaign. https://kansasreflector.com/2026/05/04/democrat-running-for-u-s-senate-receives-1-million-in-donations-in-campaigns-first-week/ and https://www.kcur.org/politics-elections-and-government/2026-10-21/control-of-the-senate-goes-through-kansas-marshall-and-hamilton-clash-at-last-debate
- **Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it.** Marshall's camp ties him to Schumer and national Democrats and attacks his handling of a 2005 church camp report, calling him unfit; Hamilton says the inquiry was inconclusive and he should have called police. https://kansasreflector.com/2026/10/05/roger-marshalls-attack-ad-against-adam-hamilton-contains-unauthorized-image-of-children/ and https://www.kcur.org/politics-elections-and-government/2026-10-21/control-of-the-senate-goes-through-kansas-marshall-and-hamilton-clash-at-last-debate
- **Strongest coalition.** Unaffiliated voters, about 29 percent of Kansas registrants; Emerson in September had him up 42 to 27 among independents and 45 to 43 overall. https://time.com/article/2026/10/07/why-kansas-has-emerged-as-a-new-battleground-state-and-why-it-matters/
- **Farm opening.** The Kansas Livestock Association declined to endorse Marshall this cycle and farmers are angry over tariffs and diesel, though many still distrust Democrats on farming. https://www.kcur.org/news/2026-10-19/kansas-farmers-ranchers-roger-marshall-donald-trump-midterm
- **Recent event.** Cook moved the race to Toss Up on October 6, 2026, and Trump rallied near Wichita for Marshall on October 19. https://time.com/article/2026/10/07/why-kansas-has-emerged-as-a-new-battleground-state-and-why-it-matters/ and https://www.kcur.org/politics-elections-and-government/2026-10-21/control-of-the-senate-goes-through-kansas-marshall-and-hamilton-clash-at-last-debate
- **Money edge.** He outraised Marshall nearly three to one through September 30, but Marshall's side had nearly ten times the ad reservations as of October 2. https://votelog.org/investigations/kansas-senate-general-money and https://time.com/article/2026/10/07/why-kansas-has-emerged-as-a-new-battleground-state-and-why-it-matters/
